comparator.name: Ancient Near Eastern Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product assigns 60 EC to each of three years for The Ancient Near Eastern World route. It displays 180 EC, but four identical module codes recur in different years: Seminar History of the Ancient Near East (5532VGONOY), From Aram to Tel Aviv (5531VATY), Material Culture of Ancient Egypt (5531VMCEY), and History of the Modern Middle East (5851VHMMEY). A student cannot earn the same module twice. After selecting the first-listed 10-EC second-year Ancient History option and counting each module code once, the published route supports only 160 unique EC. The route page and programme regulations do not identify distinct replacements for the repeated 20 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Ancient Near Eastern Studies programme. Leiden publishes four formal routes: Assyriology, Egyptology, Hebrew and Aramaic, and The Ancient Near Eastern World. The latter is the broad route spanning Egypt, the Levant, Mesopotamia, Anatolia and the Mediterranean, and is selected on academic identity before considering UCR fit.

exception.reason: The current official 2026–27 route product displays 180 EC but repeats four identical 5-EC module codes across different years. Counting those modules twice would falsely certify 20 EC. Neither the parent programme product nor the programme-regulations page identifies distinct replacement modules, so a coherent complete 180-EC comparator pathway cannot be established from the current official sources.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported unique curriculum totals 160 EC. Its established subject identity is nevertheless clear: Ancient Near Eastern history, written sources and languages; Hebrew and Aramaic cultural history; Egyptian material culture; Levantine archaeology; Mesopotamian religion; papyrology; heritage and museology; broader ancient Mediterranean study; a thesis seminar and final thesis; and 30 EC open elective space. The unresolved 20 EC prevents the complete-comparator evaluation required before deciding whether UCR can supply a defensible 24-course match. Revisit the UCR comparison after Leiden corrects the repeated modules or publishes distinct replacements.
